**Site Plan and Development Specification (Sheet 3 of 5)**
**Drawing Ref: AES/2025/SP/03 Rev D**

The following specification is extracted from the approved drawings and supporting documents submitted with the application. This sheet covers the overall development footprint, building heights, access arrangements, and landscaping proposals. It should be read in conjunction with the Design and Access Statement (Ref: AES/2025/DAS/02 Rev B) and the Landscape Strategy (Ref: AES/2025/LS/01 Rev A).

**1. Development Footprint**

The total area of land to be developed, comprising the built form, hardstanding, private gardens, and internal access roads, is set out in the table below. This figure has been agreed with the Council’s Planning Officers and is the current approved development footprint for the site.

| Land Use | Area (m²) |

| Public open space (including attenuation basin) | 280 |

Acorn Estates development footprint is 3200 m2. Record status: current. This is the figure upon which the submitted drainage strategy, ecological mitigation, and open space calculations are based. No further land within the application boundary will be subject to development works.

**2. Building Heights**

The proposed dwellings are predominantly two-storey, with a limited number of two-and-a-half storey units located at key junction points to provide architectural interest. The maximum ridge height does not exceed 9.8 metres above finished ground level. The eaves height is set at a maximum of 5.2 metres. The finished floor level of the ground floor will be set a minimum of 300mm above the 1 in 100 year plus climate change flood level, as per the Environment Agency consultation response dated 12 May 2025.

Plot types and their respective heights are detailed on Drawing Ref: AES/2025/SP/04 Rev C. A schedule of the two-and-a-half storey units is provided below for reference:

**3. Access Arrangements**

Vehicular access to the site will be provided via a single new priority junction onto Meadowbrook Link, located approximately 120 metres north of the existing roundabout. The junction design is in accordance with Manual for Streets and has been subject to a Stage 1 Road Safety Audit (Ref: RSA/2025/01). The audit raised no fundamental safety concerns. The access road will be 5.5 metres wide with a 2.0 metre footway on the western side, continuing along the site frontage.

A secondary emergency access point is proposed at the north-eastern corner of the site, connecting to the existing public footpath network. This access will be gated and used only for emergency vehicles. The gates will be set back 10 metres from the highway to allow vehicles to clear the carriageway before stopping.
